q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is August 24, 2026. NVIDIA will release Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026 (per the research). This means resolution occurs in approximately **2 days**. The guidance will be announced at that earnings release.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research provides explicit, very recent guidance issued on May 20, 2026:
- **Forward guidance for Q2 FY2027: $91.0 billion ± 2%**
- This creates a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion
- Wall Street analyst consensus is ~$91.9 billion (within the guided range)

With only 2 days until the earnings release and official guidance already publicly stated, the probability that NVIDIA announces guidance at or very near $91.0 billion is extremely high. Companies rarely, if ever, dramatically revise forward guidance between the time they initially provide it and when they formally release earnings just 2 days later—that would be a major red flag event requiring substantial market-moving developments.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- A significant negative development in data center demand or supply chain (would require material deterioration in just 3 months since Q1 results)
- Unexpected geopolitical event affecting export controls or China strategy
- Major customer slowdown announcement
- Severe macro downturn signal
- However, these would be extraordinary circumstances unlikely to emerge without warning in a 2-day window

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected sequential momentum from Q1's $81.6B (11% sequential growth already baked into $91B guidance)
- Better-than-expected enterprise demand
- Positive China-related developments (guidance explicitly excludes China revenue)
- However, if guidance were to be raised this dramatically, there would typically be signals beforehand

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research:
- Q1 FY2027 actual: $81.6 billion
- Q2 FY2027 guidance issued May 20, 2026: $91.0 billion ± 2%
- Q2 FY2026 (year-ago comparison): $46.7 billion
- Wall Street consensus: ~$91.9 billion

This implies ~11% sequential growth from Q1 to Q2, with analyst estimates clustering tightly around the midpoint of the official guidance range.

## Analysis

The stated guidance of $91.0B ± 2% is extremely specific and recent (issued just 3 months before the earnings release). With only 2 days remaining and no material adverse developments mentioned in the research, the most probable outcome is that NVIDIA announces guidance very close to this $91.0 billion figure.

The ± 2% guidance range ($89.2B–$92.8B) represents management's comfort zone. The central estimate should reflect this midpoint, with realistic tails extending slightly beyond the stated range to account for:
- Possibility of a modest beat (>$92.8B) if momentum was stronger
- Possibility of a modest miss (<$89.2B) if there were unexpected headwinds

However, given how recent and explicit the guidance is, and how tightly analyst consensus clusters within it, I should center my forecast on the stated $91.0 billion with relatively tight confidence intervals.

**Distribution reasoning:**
- 10th percentile (downside risk): ~$88.5 billion (slightly below the guided floor, accounting for rare downside surprise)
- 50th percentile (median/most likely): ~$91.0 billion (the stated guidance midpoint)
- 90th percentile (upside potential): ~$93.5 billion (modestly above the guided ceiling, accounting for rare upside surprise)

Low (10th percentile): 88500000000

High (90th percentile): 93500000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is \$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). This range sets the ceiling near \$92.8 billion and the floor near \$89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate is approximately \$91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

This guidance implies a significant year-over-year increase from the \$46.7 billion reported in the Q2 FY2026 [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The outlook explicitly does not assume any data center compute revenue from China [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). NVIDIA reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of \$81.6 billion [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027), suggesting a sequential growth slowdown to about 11% for Q2 FY2027 from 20% in Q1 FY2027 [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The company will release its Q2 FY2027 earnings report on August 26, 2026 [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).
